glasses_felix: I assumed a static location or simple progression. Actually, it was at nightstand_b1 in the early morning (07:45) and armchair_l1 late at night (22:59). Pattern: Location depends heavily on time of day. Check nightstand_b1 for early morning queries and armchair_l1 for evening/night queries. Do not default to bathroom spots.

glass_felix: I assumed it stayed at kitchen_table_k1 or moved to cupboard_k1. Actually, it was at kitchen_table_k1 in the afternoon (14:15) and sink_k1 late at night (22:59). Pattern: The glass shifts between kitchen spots based on immediate use. Check kitchen_table_k1 for afternoon queries and sink_k1 for late night queries. Do not default to counter_k1 or cupboard_k1 without specific evidence.

mug_felix: I assumed a static location at kitchen_table_k1. Actually, it was at desk_b1 in the afternoon (14:53). Pattern: Felix takes his mug to his study area (desk_b1) when he is at home studying after classes. Check kitchen_table_k1 for early morning, desk_b1 for afternoon/evening.

tablet_felix: I assumed it was at nightstand_b1. Actually, it was at kitchen_table_k1 in the morning. Pattern: Felix uses the kitchen table for his tablet in the morning. Check kitchen_table_k1.

book_felix: I assumed it was at nightstand_b1. Actually, it was at armchair_l1 late at night. Pattern: Felix reads in the living room, leaving the book on the armchair. Check armchair_l1 for evening/night queries.

General Note: My default assumption that Felix’s items move to the bedroom (nightstand_b1) at night is incorrect. He frequently leaves items in the living room (armchair, coffee table) or kitchen (table, cupboard, counter) depending on his activity. Do not default to nightstand_b1. Check living room and kitchen spots first for evening queries. For the mug specifically, distinguish between morning (kitchen) and afternoon (desk) locations.
